118.     if (edit?.op === "remove") continue; // hard removal — see doc comment
119. 
120.     const row = edit ? edit.patch : entry.row; // full replace, never a merge
121. 
122.     rows.push({
123.       rowId: entry.rowId,
124.       row,
125.       origin: "baseline",
126.       edited: edit !== undefined,
127.       softDeleted: softDelete?.isDeleted(row) ?? false,
128.     });
129.   }
130. 
131.   // 2. Adds, in edit-log order. Two guards:
132.   //    - `editByRowId.get(edit.rowId) !== edit` skips an entry a LATER
133.   //      entry for the same rowId superseded. `applyEditToLog` never
134.   //      produces duplicates, but a restored draft's per-record
135.   //      validation admits them; resolving both loops through the same
136.   //      last-write map keeps them agreeing about a rowId's content.
137.   //    - `baselineRowIds.has(edit.rowId)` skips a rowId loop 1 already
138.   //      emitted — see the collision note in the doc comment.
139.   for (const edit of log) {
140.     if (editByRowId.get(edit.rowId) !== edit) continue;
141.     if (edit.op !== "add") continue;
142.     if (baselineRowIds.has(edit.rowId)) continue;
143. 
144.     rows.push({
145.       rowId: edit.rowId,
146.       row: edit.patch,
147.       origin: "added",
148.       edited: true,
149.       softDeleted: softDelete?.isDeleted(edit.patch) ?? false,
150.     });
151.   }
152. 
153.   // 3. `baseline === undefined` means the query is loading or errored,
154.   //    NOT "the server confirmed zero rows" — an unmatched `update` is
155.   //    unresolved, not a confirmed orphan. Render it from its own patch
156.   //    (already the complete row) so a restored draft stays visible — and
157.   //    still submittable — during the loading window. `add`s were already
158.   //    emitted unconditionally by step 2; a `remove` has nothing to
159.   //    render. `origin` is "baseline" so the row doesn't visually flip
160.   //    when the real baseline arrives and confirms it.
161.   if (baseline === undefined) {
162.     for (const edit of log) {
163.       if (editByRowId.get(edit.rowId) !== edit) continue;
164.       if (edit.op !== "update") continue;
165. 
166.       rows.push({
167.         rowId: edit.rowId,
168.         row: edit.patch,
169.         origin: "baseline",
170.         edited: true,
171.         softDeleted: softDelete?.isDeleted(edit.patch) ?? false,
172.       });
173.     }
174.   }
175. 
176.   // 4. Display sort — output only.
177.   if (displayOrder) {
178.     rows.sort((a, b) => displayOrder(a.row, b.row));
179.   }
180. 
181.   return rows;
182. }

185.  * Names the rowIds {@link projectRows} silently drops: a restored edit
186.  * whose baseline row vanished server-side must be LISTED to the
187.  * clinician, not just disappear. Computed over the identical
188.  * `(baseline, log)` inputs `projectRows` takes, so the two can never
189.  * disagree about which edits are showing versus orphaned.
190.  *
191.  * `undefined` baseline returns `[]`: unresolved is not confirmed-gone —
192.  * the same conservatism `resolveChanges` applies.
193.  *
194.  * The predicate is `op !== "add" && !baselineRowIds.has(rowId)` —
195.  * deliberately NOT "not rendered", which would also flag the clinician's
196.  * own remove of an added row and every ordinary `add`.
197.  *
198.  * Resolved through the same last-write dedup `resolveChanges` uses
199.  * ({@link dedupeEditsFirstAppearance}), so a malformed log with two
200.  * entries for one rowId is reported once.
201.  *
202.  * Pure: never mutates its inputs; returns a fresh array.
203.  */
204. export function findOrphanRowIds<TRow extends object>(
205.   baseline: readonly BaselineRow<TRow>[] | undefined,
206.   log: EditLog<TRow>,
207. ): readonly RowId[] {
208.   if (baseline === undefined) return [];
209.   const baselineRowIds = new Set<RowId>(baseline.map((entry) => entry.rowId));
210. 
211.   const orphanRowIds: RowId[] = [];
212.   for (const edit of dedupeEditsFirstAppearance(log)) {
213.     if (edit.op !== "add" && !baselineRowIds.has(edit.rowId)) {
214.       orphanRowIds.push(edit.rowId);
215.     }
216.   }
217.   return orphanRowIds;
218. }
219. 
220. /**
221.  * Drops every {@link findOrphanRowIds} entry from `log`: what remains is
222.  * exactly what `projectRows` still renders (plus what it presumes during
223.  * the loading window) — never intent about a row the complete, known
224.  * baseline has confirmed gone.
225.  *
226.  * This lives at the hook, not the compose/submit seam: `toRequests` and
227.  * `resolveChanges` never hold a baseline at submit time (`composeBatch`
228.  * is pure, with no query-cache access), so `useStructuredRows` — the one
229.  * place `baseline` and `edits` coexist — must prune before its `commit`
230.  * write, or a stale draft's confirmed-gone edit reaches `toRequests`.
231.  *
232.  * Deliberately NOT the clinician's `removeRow` path: no soft-delete
233.  * marker is written and no request is implied — the entry is simply
234.  * excised, exactly as it already visually is. During the loading window
235.  * (`baseline` undefined) this is a no-op.
236.  *
237.  * Pure; returns the SAME `log` reference when nothing is dropped, so a
238.  * caller can skip a write on reference equality.
239.  */
240. export function pruneOrphanEdits<TRow extends object>(
241.   baseline: readonly BaselineRow<TRow>[] | undefined,
242.   log: EditLog<TRow>,
243. ): EditLog<TRow> {
244.   const orphanRowIds = findOrphanRowIds(baseline, log);
245.   if (orphanRowIds.length === 0) return log;
246.   const orphanSet = new Set(orphanRowIds);
247.   return log.filter((edit) => !orphanSet.has(edit.rowId));
248. }
249. 
250. /**
251.  * Restricts an edit log to at most the ONE rowId {@link projectRows}
252.  * would show as `rows[0]` for the same `(baseline, log)` pair.
253.  *
254.  * Why: singleton mode only ever SHOWS `rows[0]`, but nothing upstream
255.  * stops the log from holding a second rowId — an `initialEdits` seed
256.  * writes an `add` under `singletonRowId`, an `add` is never an orphan,
257.  * and if a real baseline row for the same question resolves under its
258.  * OWN server id while that seed is still in the log, the two coexist: a
259.  * caller writing `edits` from every projected row would silently submit
260.  * BOTH on Save. This names the one rowId that belongs in a singleton's
261.  * committed state so `commit` can filter to it.
262.  *
263.  * Unreachable for every type shipped so far (each singleton either has no
264.  * real baseline at all, or keys its baseline row with the same id passed
265.  * as `singletonRowId`) — closed by construction rather than left as a
266.  * trap for the next singleton.
267.  *
268.  * Keeps whichever rowId {@link projectRows} shows FIRST, so "the one
269.  * row" is defined by the exact projection the clinician sees.
270.  *
271.  * Pure; returns the SAME `log` reference when there is nothing to drop —
272.  * same convention as {@link pruneOrphanEdits}.
273.  */
274. export function truncateToSingletonRow<TRow extends object>(
275.   baseline: readonly BaselineRow<TRow>[] | undefined,
276.   log: EditLog<TRow>,
277.   options: ProjectRowsOptions<TRow> = {},
278. ): EditLog<TRow> {
279.   if (log.length === 0) return log;
280.   // Deliberately checks the FULL PROJECTION's row count, not `log.length`
281.   // — a baseline can contribute rows the log never mentions at all (the
282.   // exact bug shape this function exists for: a real baseline row under
283.   // its own id, plus a single seeded `add` under a DIFFERENT id, is a
284.   // one-entry log that still projects TWO rows).
285.   const rows = projectRows(baseline, log, options);
286.   if (rows.length <= 1) return log; // nothing to truncate
287.   const keepRowId = rows[0]?.rowId;
288.   // No row projects at all (e.g. every entry is an orphan against a known
289.   // baseline) — nothing to keep, but also nothing this function should
290.   // invent an opinion about; leave `log` untouched for whatever else
291.   // (orphan pruning) already handles that case. Unreachable alongside
292.   // `rows.length > 1` in practice (a non-empty `rows` always has a
293.   // `rows[0]`) — kept as a defensive, honest `undefined` check rather than
294.   // a non-null assertion.
295.   if (keepRowId === undefined) return log;
296.   const truncated = log.filter((edit) => edit.rowId === keepRowId);
297.   return truncated.length === log.length ? log : truncated;
298. }

29.  * the clinician's own edit; it must start from `{ ...patch, ... }` (or
30.  * return `patch` unchanged when there is nothing to derive). Verified by
31.  * execution: `rowMutations.test.ts`'s "CONTRACT PIN" case reproduces the
32.  * drop.
33.  */
34. export function mergePatch<TRow extends object>(
35.   current: TRow,
36.   patch: Partial<TRow>,
37.   normalizePatch?: (row: TRow, patch: Partial<TRow>) => Partial<TRow>,
38. ): TRow {
39.   // `?? patch`: a `normalizePatch` returning `undefined`/`null` is
40.   // type-illegal for typed callers but reachable from a plugin definition
41.   // crossing the `unknown` boundary at runtime. Without the fallback,
42.   // `{ ...current, ...undefined }` spreads nothing and the clinician's
43.   // edit is silently dropped.
44.   const derived = normalizePatch?.(current, patch) ?? patch;
45.   return { ...current, ...derived } as TRow;
46. }
47. 
48. // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
49. // removeRow / clearRow
50. // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
51. 
52. /**
53.  * Decides what `removeRow(rowId)` (and the singleton's `clearRow`, over
54.  * `rows[0]`) records — one user-facing affordance, two outcomes:
55.  *
56.  *  - A baseline row with `softDelete` configured ⇒ an ordinary `update`
57.  *    carrying the marker merged onto the row's CURRENT (possibly already
58.  *    edited) content — the row stays on screen, `softDeleted`, and
59.  *    un-removing later is just another update.
60.  *  - Anything else (an added row — annihilated by the reducer, it never
61.  *    reached the server — or a type with true delete semantics, or no
62.  *    `softDelete` configured) ⇒ `remove`, carrying the row's last-known
63.  *    content in `patch`.
64.  *
65.  * Loading-window note: a row synthesized while `baseline` is `undefined`
66.  * carries `origin: "baseline"`, so removing it with `softDelete`
67.  * configured records a soft-delete `update`, not a hard `remove` — a
68.  * clinician acting on a row they believe is real shouldn't have their
69.  * remove escalate to a hard delete the instant the baseline loads and
70.  * agrees with them.
71.  */
72. export function resolveRemoveIntent<TRow extends object>(
73.   entry: ProjectedRow<TRow>,
74.   softDelete: SoftDeleteDescriptor<TRow> | undefined,
75. ): RowEdit<TRow> {
76.   if (entry.origin === "baseline" && softDelete) {
77.     return {
78.       rowId: entry.rowId,
79.       op: "update",
80.       patch: { ...entry.row, ...softDelete.patch },
81.     };
82.   }
83.   return { rowId: entry.rowId, op: "remove", patch: entry.row };
84. }
85. 
86. // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
87. // setRow
88. // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
89. 
90. export interface ResolveSetRowInput<TRow extends object> {
91.   /** `rows[0]?.row` — the singleton's current content, if any row exists
92.    *  yet (baseline row, or an `add` already recorded). */
93.   currentRow: TRow | undefined;
94.   /** `rows[0]?.rowId`. Always defined exactly when `currentRow` is. */
95.   currentRowId: RowId | undefined;
96.   patch: Partial<TRow>;
97.   /** Required when no row exists yet — a create-only singleton's very
98.    *  first `setRow` call. */
99.   createSeed: (() => TRow) | undefined;
100.   singletonRowId: RowId;
101.   normalizePatch?: (row: TRow, patch: Partial<TRow>) => Partial<TRow>;
102.   /** For the thrown error's message only, when `createSeed` is required
103.    *  but missing. */
104.   questionId: string;
105. }
106. 
107. /**
108.  * Decides what `setRow(patch)` records:
109.  *
110.  *  1. A row already exists (baseline row present, or an `add` already
111.  *     recorded) ⇒ an ordinary `update` against ITS rowId; the reducer's
112.  *     coalescing keeps it an `add` when that is what the existing entry
113.  *     is — this function needn't know which.
114.  *  2. No row yet ⇒ the first-ever creation of a create-only singleton.
115.  *     `createSeed` is required here: a missing one is a caller
116.  *     misconfiguration and throws immediately rather than silently
117.  *     no-oping.
118.  */
119. export function resolveSetRow<TRow extends object>(
120.   input: ResolveSetRowInput<TRow>,
121. ): RowEdit<TRow> {
122.   const {
123.     currentRow,
124.     currentRowId,
125.     patch,
126.     createSeed,
127.     singletonRowId,
128.     normalizePatch,
129.     questionId,
130.   } = input;
131. 
132.   if (currentRow !== undefined && currentRowId !== undefined) {
133.     return {
134.       rowId: currentRowId,
135.       op: "update",
136.       patch: mergePatch(currentRow, patch, normalizePatch),
137.     };
138.   }
139. 
140.   if (!createSeed) {
141.     throw new Error(
142.       `useStructuredRows(${questionId}): mode:"single" with no baseline row requires createSeed`,
143.     );
144.   }
145.   const seed = createSeed();
146.   return {
147.     rowId: singletonRowId,
148.     op: "add",
149.     patch: mergePatch(seed, patch, normalizePatch),
150.   };
151. }
152. 
153. // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
154. // initialEdits — the one-shot seed's latch decision
155. // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
156. 
157. /**
158.  * Decides what the one-shot `initialEdits` seed effect should do THIS
159.  * render. Because `patch` is the COMPLETE row, a seed that patches a
160.  * baseline row (e.g. encounter's `?toDischarge`) cannot be constructed
161.  * until the baseline query resolves — `initialEdits` is necessarily
162.  * `undefined` on the first render, so latching unconditionally on the
163.  * first run would drop the intent permanently.
164.  *
165.  * Three outcomes:
166.  *  - `"skip"` — `edits` already has content (a restored draft, or any
167.  *    prior activity). Final: never seed. A restored draft always wins.
168.  *  - `"wait"` — `edits` empty AND `initialEdits` has no content yet. Do
169.  *    NOT latch; try again on a future render.
170.  *  - `"seed"` — `edits` empty, `initialEdits` has content: apply now,
171.  *    then latch. (The caller latches only on `"skip"`/`"seed"`, never on
172.  *    `"wait"`.)
173.  */
174. export type InitialEditsSeedDecision = "seed" | "wait" | "skip";
175. 
176. export function decideInitialEditsSeed<TRow extends object>(
177.   edits: EditLog<TRow>,
178.   initialEdits: EditLog<TRow> | undefined,
179. ): InitialEditsSeedDecision {
180.   if (edits.length > 0) return "skip";
181.   if (!initialEdits?.length) return "wait";
182.   return "seed";
183. }
184.

5. # React Components Instructions
6. 
7. ## Import Path Conventions
8. - Use path aliases: `@/components/`, `@/types/`, `@/lib/`, `@/pages/`
9. - Import order: External packages → `@/components/ui/` → `@/components/` → `@/CAREUI/` → `@/types/` → `@/lib/` → relative imports
10. - Use named exports from `lucide-react` for icons (e.g., `import { SettingsIcon } from "lucide-react"`)
11. - Import `useTranslation` from `react-i18next` for internationalization
12. 
13. ## Component Architecture Patterns
14. - Healthcare domain: Feature-based organization - Components grouped by Patient/, Facility/, Medication/, etc.
15. - React 19.1.1 hooks: Functional components only - Use React 19.1.1 hooks pattern
16. - TypeScript interfaces: Props interfaces - Always define PatientInfoCardProps, etc.
17. - Handle prefix: Event handlers - handleSubmit, handleTagsUpdate, handlePatientSelect
18. 
19. ## UI Component System
20. - shadcn/ui components: Primary UI - Button, Card, Badge, etc. from `@/components/ui/`
21. - Healthcare-specific: CAREUI custom - Calendar, WeekdayCheckbox, Zoom from `@/CAREUI/`
22. - Button variants: Use `buttonVariants` from `@/components/ui/button` with CVA patterns
23. - Card structure: Follow `<Card><CardHeader>` pattern for consistent layouts
24. 
25. ## Healthcare-Specific Patterns
26. - Patient data: Use `PatientRead` type from `@/types/emr/patient/patient`
27. - Tag system: Implement `TagAssignmentSheet` with `TagEntityType` for patient/facility tags
28. - Hover cards: Use `PatientHoverCard` for patient info overlays
29. - Badge usage: Display patient status, facility capacity, medication dosage with color variants
30. 
31. ## Styling with Tailwind CSS 4.1.3
32. - Class variance authority: Use `cva()` for variant-based component styling
33. - Utility function: Use `cn()` from `@/lib/utils` for conditional classes
34. - Color system: Follow primary-700, gray-900, red-500 pattern with dark mode variants
35. - Shadow system: Use shadow-sm, shadow-xs for elevation
36. - Focus states: Include `focus-visible:ring-1` and `focus-visible:outline-hidden`
37. 
38. ## State Management Integration
39. - Server state: React Query - Use `@tanstack/react-query` for facility data, patient records
40. - UI state: Local state - useState for UI state, useCallback for event handlers
41. - Controlled inputs: Form state - Handle controlled inputs with proper TypeScript typing
42. - Async operations: Loading states - Implement loading, error, and success states
43. 
44. ## Internationalization (i18n)
45. - Translation hook: Use `const { t } = useTranslation()` pattern
46. - Text content: Wrap all user-facing text in `t("key.path")`
47. - Healthcare terminology: Use consistent medical term translations
48. - Date formatting: Use `date-fns` with locale support for medical timestamps
49. 
50. ## Accessibility for Healthcare
51. - ARIA labels: Critical for medical data (patient names, vital signs, medication alerts)
52. - Keyboard navigation: Essential for clinical workflows and emergency situations
53. - Screen reader support: Proper heading hierarchy for medical records
54. - Color contrast: Meet WCAG AA standards for clinical environments

 *

 * unknown — never a partial array standing in for "loading".
 */
export interface ProjectRowsOptions<TRow extends object> {
  /**
   * How a type marks — instead of deletes — a baseline row's removal.
   * See `SoftDeleteDescriptor` in `./types` for the full contract.
   *
   * Read here only via `isDeleted`, to decide `ProjectedRow.softDeleted`
   * for whatever row content is already on screen — a row can be flagged
   * because its baseline data already carries the marker (soft-deleted in
   * an earlier session) just as much as because this session's edit added
   * it. `projectRows` never writes the marker itself; that is
   * `removeRow`'s job.
   */
  softDelete?: SoftDeleteDescriptor<TRow>;
  /**
   * DISPLAY ONLY. Applied as a stable sort over the canonical order
   * (baseline order, then added rows in edit-log order). Nothing
   * downstream reads row order — requests are built from the edit log,
   * identity from `rowId` — so this sort can never reach the edit log, a
   * request body, or a rowId.
   */
  displayOrder?: (a: TRow, b: TRow) => number;
}

/**
 * Computes what the clinician SEES for one structured section: baseline
 * (complete fetched server-row set, or `undefined` while unknown) plus
 * the pending edit log. This is what `values[0].value` carries for every

 * readonly renderers and server-draft dumps all read the array this
 * returns. Pure: never mutates `baseline` or `log`.

 *

 *    position never depends on whether it was edited. An `op: "remove"`
 *    edit hides the row outright (a marking type's `removeRow` records an
 *    `update`, never a `remove`, so this branch is a genuine delete). Any

 * 2. Added rows, in edit-log order — stable across a baseline refetch. An
 *    `add` whose rowId step 1 already emitted is SKIPPED: a restored
 *    draft can carry an `add` recorded before the server row existed

 *    with the add's patch as its content, rather than one rowId rendering
 *    as two rows.

 * 3. When `baseline` is a known array, every remaining `update`/`remove`
 *    is an orphan — intent about a row the complete baseline lacks — and
 *    is never rendered; {@link findOrphanRowIds} names these. When
 *    `baseline` is `undefined` (loading/errored), an unmatched `update`
 *    is unresolved, not orphaned — see step 3 in the implementation.

 */

21. import type { StructuredEdit } from "@/types/questionnaire/structured";
22. 
23. /**
24.  * The definition object is required here — every row the editor creates
25.  * comes from a picked `ChargeItemDefinitionRead` (`newChargeItemRow`) —
26.  * while the wider `ChargeItemQuestionRow` arm keeps both display objects
27.  * optional, since it also describes legacy responses and old drafts where
28.  * they may be absent.
29.  */
30. export type ChargeItemRow = ChargeItemQuestionRow & {
31.   charge_item_definition_object: ChargeItemDefinitionRead;
32. };
33. 
34. /**
35.  * Assistant write guard. `charge_item_definition_object`/
36.  * `performer_actor_object` are passthrough, id-keyed-only schemas: an
37.  * assistant only ever copies one verbatim from a prior pick, never authors
38.  * the full `ChargeItemDefinitionRead`/`UserReadMinimal` shape by hand. Every
39.  * other field is `.strict()`.
40.  */
41. export const rowSchema = z
42.   .object({
43.     charge_item_definition: nonEmptyString,
44.     quantity: z.string(),
45.     encounter: z.string().optional(),
46.     patient: z.string().optional(),
47.     service_resource: z.enum(ChargeItemServiceResource).optional(),
48.     service_resource_id: z.string().optional(),
49.     performer_actor: z.string().optional(),
50.     account: z.string().optional(),
51.     charge_item_definition_object: displayObjectSchema(["slug", "title"]),
52.     performer_actor_object: userDisplaySchema.optional(),
53.   })
54.   .strict();
55. 
56. /**
57.  * A charge-item section is a LIST whose rows are born whole
58.  * (`newChargeItemRow`): there is no "half filled" state, so no `isEmptyRow`
59.  * predicate to keep in sync with a submission filter. Whatever `rows` holds
60.  * is what the clinician sees and exactly the set `toRequests` compiles
61.  * requests for.
62.  */
63. export const projectValues: ProjectValues<ChargeItemRow> = (rows) =>
64.   rows.length === 0 ? [] : [{ type: "charge_item", value: [...rows] }];
65. 
66. /**
67.  * A freshly picked definition becomes a row: quantity defaults to `"1"`,
68.  * `encounter` comes from context (a charge item is always billed to the
69.  * encounter being filled), and the definition's `slug` is the wire identity
70.  * `apply_charge_item_defs/` expects. The definition object rides along on
71.  * the row — not fetched a second time — so a restored draft or the list can
72.  * repaint title/price straight from the response.
73.  */
74. export function newChargeItemRow(
75.   definition: ChargeItemDefinitionRead,
76.   encounterId: string,
77. ): ChargeItemRow {
78.   return {
79.     quantity: "1",
80.     encounter: encounterId,
81.     charge_item_definition: definition.slug,
82.     charge_item_definition_object: definition,
83.   };
84. }
85. 
86. /**
87.  * The single place display objects are stripped before the wire. The exact
88.  * remaining key set is pinned by a dedicated test, not inferred from this
89.  * comment.
90.  */
91. export function stripDisplay(
92.   row: ChargeItemRow,
93. ): ApplyChargeItemDefinitionRequest {
94.   const {
95.     charge_item_definition_object: _definition,
96.     performer_actor_object: _performer,
97.     ...request
98.   } = row;
99.   return request;
100. }
101. 
102. export async function toRequests(
103.   edits: readonly StructuredEdit<ChargeItemRow>[],
104.   { facilityId, questionId }: StructuredRequestContext,
105. ): Promise<StructuredBatchEntry[]> {
106.   if (!facilityId) return [];
107.   // Create-only: no server row is ever fetched for this type, so the baseline
108.   // is permanently empty — stated as an explicit empty Map because omitting
109.   // `baseline` means "still loading or errored" per
110.   // `ResolveChangesOptions.baseline`, which is not the fact here.
111.   //
112.   // `updates`/`removes` are deliberately not merged into the request body:
113.   // `apply_charge_item_defs/` is create-only (no verb for an update), and a
114.   // remove for a rowId that never reached the server carries nothing worth
115.   // sending. Add-then-remove pairs annihilate inside the reducer before this
116.   // function ever sees them.
117.   const { creates } = resolveChanges(edits, { baseline: new Map() });
118.   if (creates.length === 0) return [];
119.   return [
120.     {
121.       url: `/api/v1/facility/${facilityId}/charge_item/apply_charge_item_defs/`,
122.       method: "POST",
123.       body: { requests: creates.map(stripDisplay) },
124.       reference_id: structuredReferenceId("charge_item", questionId),
125.     },
126.   ];
127. }
128. 
129. /** Is `quantity` a positive integer, written as the wire's plain string
130.  *  (`ApplyChargeItemDefinitionRequest.quantity: string`)? Trimmed first so
131.  *  incidental whitespace doesn't fail a value that is otherwise a clean
132.  *  integer — the same defensive trim `appointment`'s `hasValidSlot` applies
133.  *  to `slot_id`. `"0"`/negative values fail the `>= 1` check, not the regex,
134.  *  so both are reported for the same reason a clinician can act on: not a
135.  *  quantity, not "at least one". */
136. function isPositiveIntegerQuantity(quantity: string): boolean {
137.   const trimmed = quantity.trim();
138.   return /^\d+$/.test(trimmed) && Number(trimmed) >= 1;
139. }
140. 
141. /**
142.  * Row-scoped quantity predicate; the definition's `validate()` turns each
143.  * returned rowId into a blocking `QuestionValidationError`. The wire type is
144.  * a bare string (`ApplyChargeItemDefinitionRequest.quantity`) and the
145.  * editor's `<Input type="number" min={1}>` is only a browser hint, so
146.  * `""`/`"-1"`/`"abc"` are all representable — this predicate is the only
147.  * client-side gate.
148.  *
149.  * `toRequests` deliberately does NOT also filter on it: client validation
150.  * runs before request compilation and blocks the whole submit on any error,
151.  * so `toRequests` cannot run while an invalid quantity survives — and having
152.  * it silently drop the row instead would make the clinician's entry vanish
153.  * from the request with no message they can act on. Projection and submit
154.  * therefore both include a row regardless of its quantity's validity.
155.  *
156.  * A `remove` edit's quantity is never reported: the row is on its way out,
157.  * not something the clinician still needs to fix.
158.  */
159. export function invalidQuantityRowIds(
160.   edits: readonly StructuredEdit<ChargeItemRow>[],
161. ): string[] {
162.   return edits
163.     .filter(
164.       (edit) =>
165.         edit.op !== "remove" && !isPositiveIntegerQuantity(edit.patch.quantity),
166.     )
167.     .map((edit) => edit.rowId);
168. }
169.

1. import { format } from "date-fns";
2. import { z } from "zod";
3. 
4. import { resolveChanges } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/core/changes";
5. import type {
6.   BaselineRow,
7.   ProjectValues,
8.   SoftDeleteDescriptor,
9. } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/core/types";
10. import {
11.   onsetSchema,
12.   userDisplaySchema,
13. } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/shared/rowSchemaPrimitives";
14. import type {
15.   StructuredBatchEntry,
16.   StructuredRequestContext,
17. } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/types";
18. import { structuredReferenceId } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/types";
19. import { CodeSchema, type Code } from "@/types/base/code/code";
20. import type {
21.   Diagnosis,
22.   DiagnosisRequest,
23. } from "@/types/emr/diagnosis/diagnosis";
24. import {
25.   DIAGNOSIS_CATEGORY,
26.   DIAGNOSIS_CLINICAL_STATUS,
27.   DIAGNOSIS_SEVERITY,
28.   DIAGNOSIS_VERIFICATION_STATUS,
29. } from "@/types/emr/diagnosis/diagnosis";
30. import type { StructuredEdit } from "@/types/questionnaire/structured";
31. 
32. /** The wire request shape doubles as the editable row shape. */
33. export type DiagnosisRow = DiagnosisRequest;
34. 
35. /**
36.  * Assistant write guard. `severity` is `.nullable()` to match
37.  * `DiagnosisRequest.severity: DiagnosisSeverity | null`. Timestamp fields
38.  * are read-only pass-through, left as plain optional strings.
39.  */
40. export const rowSchema = z
41.   .object({
42.     id: z.string().optional(),
43.     clinical_status: z.enum(DIAGNOSIS_CLINICAL_STATUS),
44.     verification_status: z.enum(DIAGNOSIS_VERIFICATION_STATUS),
45.     code: CodeSchema,
46.     severity: z.enum(DIAGNOSIS_SEVERITY).nullable(),
47.     onset: onsetSchema.optional(),
48.     recorded_date: z.string().optional(),
49.     note: z.string().optional(),
50.     category: z.enum(DIAGNOSIS_CATEGORY),
51.     encounter: z.string().min(1),
52.     created_by: userDisplaySchema.optional(),
53.     created_date: z.string().optional(),
54.     updated_date: z.string().optional(),
55.   })
56.   .strict();
57. 
58. /**
59.  * Removing a row that exists on the server flips `verification_status` to
60.  * `entered_in_error` and keeps it visible; a row that never reached the
61.  * server is dropped outright. `useStructuredRows` dispatches on this
62.  * descriptor by row origin.
63.  */
64. export const DIAGNOSIS_SOFT_DELETE: SoftDeleteDescriptor<DiagnosisRow> = {
65.   patch: { verification_status: "entered_in_error" },
66.   isDeleted: (row) => row.verification_status === "entered_in_error",
67. };
68. 
69. /**
70.  * Read shape → the row this question edits; `onset.onset_datetime` is cut
71.  * down to a bare date. Uses `date-fns` directly — `@/Utils/utils`
72.  * transitively reads `import.meta.env` via `@careConfig`, undefined under
73.  * `node --test`.
74.  */
75. export function toDiagnosisRow(diagnosis: Diagnosis): DiagnosisRow {
76.   return {
77.     id: diagnosis.id,
78.     code: diagnosis.code,
79.     clinical_status: diagnosis.clinical_status,
80.     verification_status: diagnosis.verification_status,
81.     severity: diagnosis.severity,
82.     onset: diagnosis.onset
83.       ? {
84.           ...diagnosis.onset,
85.           onset_datetime: diagnosis.onset.onset_datetime
86.             ? format(new Date(diagnosis.onset.onset_datetime), "yyyy-MM-dd")
87.             : "",
88.         }
89.       : undefined,
90.     recorded_date: diagnosis.recorded_date,
91.     category: diagnosis.category,
92.     note: diagnosis.note,
93.     encounter: diagnosis.encounter,
94.     created_by: diagnosis.created_by,
95.     created_date: diagnosis.created_date,
96.   };
97. }
98. 
99. /**
100.  * Keyed by the server id so `removeRow` distinguishes baseline
101.  * (soft-delete) from added (annihilate) rows. Callers pass `undefined`,
102.  * never `[]`, while the fetch is unresolved.
103.  */
104. export function toBaselineRows(
105.   diagnoses: readonly Diagnosis[],
106. ): BaselineRow<DiagnosisRow>[] {
107.   return diagnoses.map((diagnosis) => ({
108.     rowId: diagnosis.id,
109.     row: toDiagnosisRow(diagnosis),
110.   }));
111. }
112. 
113. /**
114.  * Legacy add-flow defaults: active/confirmed, severity "moderate",
115.  * category "encounter_diagnosis", onset today. Only the historical-record
116.  * flow can bring in a "chronic_condition" row. `encounter` is set at
117.  * creation because a row's `patch` must be the complete row.
118.  */
119. export function newDiagnosisRow(code: Code, encounterId: string): DiagnosisRow {
120.   return {
121.     code,
122.     clinical_status: "active",
123.     verification_status: "confirmed",
124.     severity: "moderate",
125.     category: "encounter_diagnosis",
126.     onset: { onset_datetime: format(new Date(), "yyyy-MM-dd") },
127.     encounter: encounterId,
128.   };
129. }
130. 
131. /** Rows are complete from creation — no empty-row filter needed; an
132.  *  empty list projects to an unanswered section. */
133. export const projectValues: ProjectValues<DiagnosisRow> = (rows) =>
134.   rows.length === 0 ? [] : [{ type: "diagnosis", value: [...rows] }];
135. 
136. /** Duplicate-guard key for `findDuplicateCandidates`, which already
137.  *  excludes soft-deleted (entered_in_error) rows from its seen set. */
138. export function diagnosisDuplicateKey(row: DiagnosisRow): string | undefined {
139.   return row.code.code || undefined;
140. }
141. 
142. function onsetTime(row: DiagnosisRow): number {
143.   // A missing onset gets a fixed rank (sorts last): the comparator must
144.   // be pure and deterministic, so no wall-clock fallback.
145.   return row.onset?.onset_datetime
146.     ? new Date(row.onset.onset_datetime).getTime()
147.     : Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY;
148. }
149. 
150. /**
151.  * Display-only onset-ascending sort, passed as `displayOrder` to
152.  * `projectRows`: it reorders the returned `ProjectedRow[]` only. The
153.  * baseline and edit log — and therefore `toRequests` — never see this
154.  * order; rows are addressed by `rowId`, never by position.
155.  */
156. export function diagnosisDisplayOrder(
157.   a: DiagnosisRow,
158.   b: DiagnosisRow,
159. ): number {
160.   return onsetTime(a) - onsetTime(b);
161. }
162. 
163. /**
164.  * Onset is frozen once a row exists on the server — editing a recorded
165.  * diagnosis's onset would rewrite clinical history. A row re-added from
166.  * history has its id stripped and is genuinely new, so its onset stays
167.  * editable.
168.  */
169. export function isOnsetFrozen(origin: "baseline" | "added"): boolean {
170.   return origin === "baseline";
171. }
172. 
173. /** Kept local rather than importing `definitions/adapt.ts`'s
174.  *  `sanitizeNote`: `model.ts` must stay React-free for `node --test`, and
175.  *  adapt.ts imports React. */
176. function sanitizeNote(note: string | undefined): string | undefined {
177.   return note?.trim() || undefined;
178. }
179. 
180. /**
181.  * Reuses a historical diagnosis as a NEW row for this encounter: the
182.  * server id is stripped — keeping it would make the upsert update the
183.  * original record in place — a null severity defaults to "moderate", and
184.  * `encounter` is re-stamped to the current encounter.
185.  */
186. export function toReusedDiagnosisRow(
187.   row: DiagnosisRow,
188.   encounterId: string,
189. ): DiagnosisRow {
190.   const { id: _id, ...rest } = row;
191.   return {
192.     ...rest,
193.     severity: rest.severity ?? "moderate",
194.     encounter: encounterId,
195.   };
196. }
197. 
198. /**
199.  * Edit log → at most one POST to the upsert endpoint. An empty edit log
200.  * yields an empty batch — dirtiness is derived from the log, so untouched
201.  * baseline rows are never re-sent.
202.  *
203.  * `resolveChanges` receives no baseline: the differ only sees the edit
204.  * log, and the hook's prune effect drops edits for rows the baseline has
205.  * proven gone before submit. A `removes` entry always carries `.row` when
206.  * a softDelete descriptor is supplied; the `flatMap` guard honors the
207.  * shared optional type instead of asserting.
208.  *
209.  * `encounter: encounterId` overrides each row's own value on purpose — a
210.  * historical row carries the encounter it was originally recorded under;
211.  * re-stamping attaches it to the current encounter (legacy submit
212.  * behavior).
213.  */
214. export async function toRequests(
215.   edits: readonly StructuredEdit<DiagnosisRow>[],
216.   { patientId, encounterId, questionId }: StructuredRequestContext,
217. ): Promise<StructuredBatchEntry[]> {
218.   if (!patientId || !encounterId) return [];
219.   const { creates, updates, removes } = resolveChanges(edits, {
220.     softDelete: DIAGNOSIS_SOFT_DELETE,
221.   });
222.   const rows = [
223.     ...creates,
224.     ...updates,
225.     ...removes.flatMap((entry) => (entry.row ? [entry.row] : [])),
226.   ];
227.   if (rows.length === 0) return [];
228.   return [
229.     {
230.       url: `/api/v1/patient/${patientId}/diagnosis/upsert/`,
231.       method: "POST",
232.       body: {
233.         datapoints: rows.map((row) => ({
234.           ...row,
235.           note: sanitizeNote(row.note),
236.           encounter: encounterId,
237.         })),
238.       },
239.       reference_id: structuredReferenceId("diagnosis", questionId),
240.     },
241.   ];
242. }
243.

1. import { z } from "zod";
2. 
3. import { resolveChanges } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/core/changes";
4. import type {
5.   BaselineRow,
6.   ProjectValues,
7. } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/core/types";
8. import { periodSchema } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/shared/rowSchemaPrimitives";
9. import type {
10.   StructuredBatchEntry,
11.   StructuredRequestContext,
12. } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/types";
13. import { structuredReferenceId } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/types";
14. import {
15.   ENCOUNTER_ADMIT_SOURCE,
16.   ENCOUNTER_CLASS,
17.   ENCOUNTER_DIET_PREFERENCE,
18.   ENCOUNTER_DISCHARGE_DISPOSITION,
19.   ENCOUNTER_PRIORITY,
20.   EncounterStatus,
21.   type EncounterClass,
22.   type EncounterDischargeDisposition,
23.   type EncounterEdit,
24.   type EncounterRead,
25. } from "@/types/emr/encounter/encounter";
26. import type { StructuredEdit } from "@/types/questionnaire/structured";
27. 
28. /**
29.  * `EncounterEdit` carries no `id` of its own — the only endpoint that
30.  * consumes it is URL-keyed (`PUT /api/v1/encounter/{id}/`). That fact
31.  * drives {@link toBaselineRows}'s rowId, {@link toRequests}' identity
32.  * filter, and why an `add` and an `update` compile to the same request.
33.  */
34. export type EncounterRow = EncounterEdit;
35. 
36. /** `Hospitalization`'s zod mirror — `.strict()`, every field optional,
37.  *  matching `Hospitalization`'s own four fields exactly. */
38. const hospitalizationSchema = z
39.   .object({
40.     re_admission: z.boolean().optional(),
41.     admit_source: z.enum(ENCOUNTER_ADMIT_SOURCE).optional(),
42.     discharge_disposition: z.enum(ENCOUNTER_DISCHARGE_DISPOSITION).optional(),
43.     diet_preference: z.enum(ENCOUNTER_DIET_PREFERENCE).optional(),
44.   })
45.   .strict();
46. 
47. /**
48.  * Runtime guard on externally authored rows. `hospitalization` accepts
49.  * `null`, matching `Hospitalization | null | undefined` — the server holds
50.  * `null` for an encounter that never had one. `external_identifier`/
51.  * `discharge_summary_advice` are `string | null` on the real type — both
52.  * `.nullable()`, not merely `.optional()`.
53.  */
54. export const rowSchema = z
55.   .object({
56.     status: z.enum(EncounterStatus),
57.     encounter_class: z.enum(ENCOUNTER_CLASS),
58.     period: periodSchema,
59.     hospitalization: hospitalizationSchema.nullable().optional(),
60.     priority: z.enum(ENCOUNTER_PRIORITY),
61.     external_identifier: z.string().nullable(),
62.     discharge_summary_advice: z.string().nullable(),
63.   })
64.   .strict();
65. 
66. /** Statuses that END an encounter, and therefore want a `period.end`. */
67. const TERMINAL_STATUSES: ReadonlySet<EncounterStatus> = new Set([
68.   EncounterStatus.DISCHARGED,
69.   EncounterStatus.COMPLETED,
70.   EncounterStatus.CANCELLED,
71.   EncounterStatus.DISCONTINUED,
72.   EncounterStatus.ENTERED_IN_ERROR,
73. ]);
74. 
75. /** Classes with no hospitalization record at all. */
76. const AMBULATORY_CLASSES: readonly EncounterClass[] = ["amb", "vr", "hh"];
77. 
78. /** Classes that DO carry one, and therefore need a discharge disposition
79.  *  once discharged. */
80. const HOSPITALIZED_CLASSES: readonly EncounterClass[] = [
81.   "imp",
82.   "obsenc",
83.   "emer",
84. ];
85. 
86. /**
87.  * Does this class carry a hospitalization record? The single authority for
88.  * this split — the editor's hospitalization panel, the derivation rules
89.  * and the validator must never disagree about which classes have one.
90.  */
91. export function isHospitalizedClass(encounterClass: EncounterClass): boolean {
92.   return HOSPITALIZED_CLASSES.includes(encounterClass);
93. }
94. 
95. /**
96.  * `EncounterRead` → the seven fields this question edits. Everything else
97.  * `EncounterRead` carries (patient, facility, tags, care team, histories,
98.  * permissions) is display data that must never ride along into a PUT
99.  * body; the exact key set is pinned by a test.
100.  */
101. export function toEncounterRow(read: EncounterRead): EncounterRow {
102.   return {
103.     status: read.status,
104.     encounter_class: read.encounter_class,
105.     period: read.period,
106.     hospitalization: read.hospitalization,
107.     priority: read.priority,
108.     external_identifier: read.external_identifier,
109.     discharge_summary_advice: read.discharge_summary_advice,
110.   };
111. }
112. 
113. /**
114.  * Exactly one baseline row, keyed by the ENCOUNTER id — not
115.  * `SINGLETON_ROW_ID`, which `core/rowIds.ts` reserves for create-only
116.  * types with no server row. This row's identity is the encounter id in the
117.  * PUT URL; keying the baseline by it lets {@link toRequests} decide from
118.  * the edit log alone whether an edit is about THIS encounter.
119.  *
120.  * Only ever called with a resolved `EncounterRead`, so the returned set is
121.  * complete. While the query is loading or errored the caller must pass
122.  * `undefined` to the hook, never `[]` — an empty array claims the server
123.  * has no rows, which reclassifies edits as data-creating and makes
124.  * `projectRows` drop every restored edit as an orphan.
125.  */
126. export function toBaselineRows(
127.   read: EncounterRead,
128.   encounterId: string,
129. ): BaselineRow<EncounterRow>[] {
130.   return [{ rowId: encounterId, row: toEncounterRow(read) }];
131. }
132. 
133. /**
134.  * Deliberately `rows[0]`, not `[...rows]`: `SingleRowController.row` hands
135.  * the editor exactly `rows[0]`, so a corrupted two-rowId log must not
136.  * project TWO encounters into `values[0].value` while the editor shows one
137.  * and {@link toRequests} PUTs one.
138.  *
139.  * No `isEmptyRow`: an encounter row always has a status, class, period and
140.  * priority — there is no blank state to clear it to. An untouched section
141.  * is silent because its EDIT LOG is empty, which {@link toRequests} checks
142.  * first.
143.  */
144. export const projectValues: ProjectValues<EncounterRow> = (rows) => {
145.   const row = rows[0];
146.   if (!row) return [];
147.   return [{ type: "encounter", value: [row] }];
148. };
149. 
150. /**
151.  * The encounter's domain derivations, one pure function applied to every
152.  * patch before it is recorded; a combined class+status edit is evaluated
153.  * against the values it is SETTING, and the one-pass fixpoint is executed
154.  * in `model.test.ts`.
155.  *
156.  * RETURN CONTRACT (`StructuredRowsOptions.normalizePatch`): the result
157.  * REPLACES `patch` before being spread onto the row, so it must start from
158.  * `{ ...patch }`. Takes its config rather than importing `@careConfig`
159.  * (`care.config.ts` reads `import.meta.env`, absent under `node --test`);
160.  * `now` is injectable so period assertions can name a value.
161.  *
162.  * Rules, in order:
163.  *  1. period.end follows the status — a terminal status with no end gets
164.  *     `now()`; an existing end is kept (a clinician-picked date is not
165.  *     re-stamped); a non-terminal status clears it, writing nothing when
166.  *     there is nothing to clear, so an unrelated edit cannot manufacture a
167.  *     period diff.
168.  *  2. An ambulatory class clears a POPULATED hospitalization to `{}` —
169.  *     never writes `{}` over a server `null`/already-`{}`, which would put
170.  *     an untouched field into the PUT body.
171.  *  3. A hospitalized class that is DISCHARGED gets a disposition — the one
172.  *     set, or the configured default.
173.  *
174.  * Deliberately NO rule re-pins `discharge_disposition` to the server value
175.  * on unrelated edits (that erased the clinician's pick mid-form); pinned
176.  * by a regression test.
177.  */
178. export function makeNormalizePatch({
179.   dischargeDisposition,
180.   now = () => new Date().toISOString(),
181. }: {
182.   // `| undefined`, matching `careConfig.defaultDischargeDisposition` (the
183.   // env var behind it is optional). Rule 3's `??` then leaves the

190.     row: EncounterRow,
191.     patch: Partial<EncounterRow>,
192.   ): Partial<EncounterRow> {

195.

197.     if (TERMINAL_STATUSES.has(next.status)) {
198.       if (!next.period.end) out.period = { ...next.period, end: now() };
199.     } else if (next.period.end) {
200.       // `end: undefined` rather than a delete: `deepEqualJson` treats an
201.       // undefined-valued key as ABSENT, so this still collapses back to a
202.       // baseline that never had an end.
203.       out.period = { ...next.period, end: undefined };
204.     }
205. 
206.     // Rules 2 and 3 — the hospitalization record follows class + status.
207.     if (AMBULATORY_CLASSES.includes(next.encounter_class)) {
208.       if (
209.         next.hospitalization &&

211.       ) {
212.         out.hospitalization = {};
213.       }
214.     } else if (
215.       isHospitalizedClass(next.encounter_class) &&
216.       next.status === EncounterStatus.DISCHARGED
217.     ) {
218.       out.hospitalization = {
219.         ...next.hospitalization,
220.         discharge_disposition:
221.           next.hospitalization?.discharge_disposition ?? dischargeDisposition,
222.       };
223.     }
224. 
225.     return out;
226.   };
227. }

231.  * hospitalized class with no disposition set. The definition turns this
232.  * into a `QuestionValidationError` on

245.   row: EncounterRow | undefined,

248.     row?.status === EncounterStatus.DISCHARGED &&

251.   );

/**
 * Structural equality over JSON-safe values — the sole judge of whether an
 * `update` edit has collapsed back to its baseline row, so a section can
 * honestly report zero pending intent. Matches `JSON.stringify` semantics
 * rather than a naive recursive `===`:
 *
 *  1. Object key order is irrelevant.
 *  2. An object key whose value is `undefined` is treated as ABSENT on
 *     both sides (`JSON.stringify` drops such keys), so a patch built as
 *     `{ ...baselineRow, someField: undefined }` compares equal to a row
 *     that was never patched.
 *
 * Deliberate edge-case decisions:
 *
 *  - `null` and `undefined` are DISTINCT: rule 2 makes an
 *    `undefined`-valued key equivalent to an absent key, never to `null`.
 *  - `NaN` equals `NaN` (two "not a number" fields are not a clinician's
 *    change) but never equals `null`, despite `JSON.stringify(NaN)`
 *    printing `null`.
 *  - Array elements are compared positionally and order-sensitively, with
 *    no undefined-as-absent normalization — rows have optional KEYS, not
 *    optional array slots, and array fields are meaningful sequences.
 *  - Non-plain objects (`Date`, `Map`, `Set`, `RegExp`, class instances,
 *    `File` — which reaches this function inside a `files` row's `add`
 *    patch) fall back to reference equality; none are JSON-safe to begin
 *    with.

 *    request object and cannot become cyclic, so a stack overflow on a
 *    cycle is a loud caller bug, not a case to silently "succeed" on.

/**
 * Structural equality over JSON-safe values — the sole judge of whether an
 * `update` edit has collapsed back to its baseline row, so that section can
 * honestly report zero pending intent (an untouched section must produce
 * zero upsert requests). Two rules make it match `JSON.stringify` rather
 * than a naive recursive `===`:
 *
 *  1. Object key order is irrelevant: `{a:1,b:2}` deepEqualJson `{b:2,a:1}`.
 *  2. An object key whose value is `undefined` is treated as ABSENT on both
 *     sides — `JSON.stringify` drops such keys, so `{a: undefined}`
 *     deepEqualJson `{}`. This is what lets a patch built as
 *     `{ ...baselineRow, someField: undefined }` compare equal to a row
 *     that was never patched at all.
 *
 * Everything below is a DELIBERATE, DOCUMENTED decision for an edge case
 * the annex leaves implicit — not left as undefined behavior:
 *
 *  - `null` and `undefined` are DISTINCT values, always. `{a: null}` is
 *    NOT deepEqualJson to `{}` or to `{a: undefined}` — rule 2 only makes
 *    an `undefined`-valued key equivalent to an ABSENT key, never to a key
 *    holding a real `null`. (`JSON.stringify({a:null})` prints a real
 *    `"a":null` member; `JSON.stringify({a:undefined})` prints nothing.)
 *
 *  - `NaN` is equal to `NaN` (unlike `===`). Two fields that both hold
 *    "not a number" is not a change a clinician made. This does NOT extend
 *    to treating `NaN` as equal to `null`, even though
 *    `JSON.stringify(NaN) === "null"` — that coincidence of the wire
 *    format is not given semantic weight here; `NaN` compares equal only
 *    to another `NaN`.
 *
 *  - `-0` is equal to `0` (both serialize to the JSON literal `0`). Plain
 *    `===` already agrees (`-0 === 0` is `true` in JS), so no special case
 *    is needed — noted here so a future refactor doesn't "fix" it away.
 *
 *  - Array elements are compared positionally with NO undefined-as-absent
 *    normalization (unlike object keys): `[undefined]` is NOT deepEqualJson
 *    to `[null]`. `JSON.stringify` does coerce an array's `undefined`
 *    element to the literal `null` on the wire, but no row shape in this
 *    codebase carries an optional ARRAY SLOT — rows have optional KEYS.
 *    Adopting the array coercion too would add a second "which values
 *    count as absent" rule for a case nothing here produces; keeping array
 *    comparison a straightforward recursive check is the simpler, safer
 *    choice.
 *
 *  - Arrays are order-sensitive: `[1,2]` is NOT deepEqualJson to `[2,1]`.
 *    A row's array fields are meaningful sequences, not sets.
 *
 *  - Anything that is not a plain object or an array — `Date`, `Map`,
 *    `Set`, `RegExp`, a class instance, or a `File` (the one non-JSON
 *    value that actually reaches this function, inside a `files` row's
 *    `add` patch — `update`/`remove` on a `files` row never carry one) —
 *    falls back to REFERENCE equality (`===`). None of these are JSON-safe
 *    to begin with (`JSON.stringify` on a `Map`/`Set` yields `"{}"`), so no
 *    attempt is made to compare their contents structurally: two distinct
 *    instances with identical-looking content are DIFFERENT unless they
 *    are the same reference.
 *
 *  - Cyclic inputs are NOT guarded against: a self-referential object
 *    recurses until the call stack overflows (`RangeError: Maximum call
 *    stack size exceeded`), unlike `JSON.stringify`, which throws a
 *    catchable `TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON`. No
 *    guard is added on purpose — every row shape in this codebase is a
 *    plain API request object (built from typed literals, `JSON.parse`,
 *    or a shallow spread) and cannot become cyclic; a cycle reaching here
 *    would mean a caller bug, not a legitimate edit-log state, so failing
 *    loudly beats silently "succeeding" on a truncated comparison.
 */

def replace_block(path: Path, start_line: int, new: str):
    lines=path.read_text().splitlines(keepends=True)
    idx=start_line-1
    # scan forward a few lines to comment start in case earlier edits shifted
    s=None
    for k in range(max(0,idx-3), min(len(lines), idx+4)):
        if '/*' in lines[k]:
            s=k; break
    if s is None:
        raise RuntimeError(f'comment start not found {path}:{start_line}')
    e=s
    while e < len(lines) and '*/' not in lines[e]:
        e+=1
    if e>=len(lines): raise RuntimeError(f'comment end not found {path}:{start_line}')
    new_lines=[l+'\n' for l in new.splitlines()]
    lines[s:e+1]=new_lines
    path.write_text(''.join(lines))
